surprises: Mantine's `disabled` on `NavLink` only adds `data-disabled` (opacity plus `pointer-events: none`) — it neither emits `aria-disabled` nor blocks `onClick`, so what actually makes a not-yet-built destination inert is the absence of `component={Link}`, not the prop that appears to disable it.

Dropping `component={Link}` is also what breaks the accessibility criterion: the element falls to an `<a>` with no href (role `generic`), where `aria-disabled` is unsupported — and the test written to prove inertness asserts exactly that missing `link` role, so it locks the defect in while passing.

`lingui compile --strict` reported 0 missing messages across all 7 locales while ja rendered the "Discover" nav header as 発見 (the noun "a discovery"); the gate proves a string exists, never that it fits its slot.

proposed_rules.diff: +- **Making a control inert by removing what makes it interactive also removes the role that can carry its state.** A Mantine `NavLink` rendered without `component={Link}` is an `<a>` with no href — role `generic`, where `aria-disabled` is unsupported and assistive tech announces plain text. Keep an explicit `role="link"`, or render `component="button"` with `disabled`. And assert the state through `getByRole(role, { name })`, never through the raw attribute: an attribute assertion passes on an element that exposes nothing.

+- **A table keyed by a union is a `Record<Union, T>` plus an explicit order tuple, never an array of `{ id: Union }`.** The array literal type-checks with members missing, so adding a variant silently drops everything under it with no compile error — exactly the failure a union was chosen to prevent. Reach for the array form only when the key genuinely is open-ended.
